absent: Numeric values of priority bounds, batch sizes, bin counts, unit width and watermark helpers not shown.
Bodies of per-vector shrink, evictable sizing, swappiness query, anon reclaim check and node state helpers not shown.
Shrinker lifecycle including registration, identifier allocation, reference helpers and info expansion not shown.
Memcg protection and event helpers, pressure notification, reclaim state flush, rotation and abort internals not shown.
Zone watermark checks, promotion marks, compaction gap sizing, fragmentation index and threshold tuning not shown beyond call sites.
Proactive reclaim mode, scan control setup, and background reclaim scheduling loop not shown.
Configuration selection between real and stubbed memcg deferred and slab paths not shown beyond the paired variants.

findings.text: Global slab shrink dispatcher serving a node and cgroup at a given priority and returning aggregate freed objects, forwarding non-root cgroups to a dedicated memcg walk and otherwise iterating the global shrinker registry.

Public compaction eligibility check for a zone at an order with watermark and zone ceiling, combining a watermark gate with a fragmentation policy for costly orders and reporting through a trace hook.

Public release routine detaching one cgroup from per-node generation lists on every node, maintaining per-generation counts and advancing the shared sequence when the current generation becomes empty.
Public conditional clearing of hopeless node state that first tests balance at an order and zone ceiling, then clears with a variant selected by whether the caller is background reclaim context.
Reclaim entry for shrinkers that first handles the disabled memcg alias where a non-root view must still run the memcg path while skipping the global walk to avoid premature out of memory handling.
Per-node multi cgroup reclaim walk that starts from a random bin of the current generation and visits every bin until termination or abort.

Initial priority is left unchanged unless control starts at default priority with a sizable reclaim target; otherwise reclaimable inactive file plus conditionally reclaimable inactive anonymous pages sizes an estimate that is clamped between half default and default to bound shrinker overshoot.

Per-shrinker scan debt is claimed atomically then augmented by fresh pressure proportional to freeable objects scaled by priority and cost, with zero cost objects treated aggressively, and the combined target is capped at twice freeable while unused debt is carried forward capped similarly.

Scanning proceeds in bounded batches while remaining work covers a full batch or covers all freeable objects under tight pressure, stopping early on a stop signal, accounting scanned versus freed separately, and yielding voluntarily between batches.

Deferred counters fold node identity to zero for non NUMA aware shrinkers and select per cgroup per node storage only when both a cgroup context and memcg awareness are present, with one configuration providing real storage and an alternate configuration stubbed to return zero.

Balance is tested bottom up over managed zones within a ceiling, using tiered promotion marks when tiering is enabled, block granularity under defrag for higher orders, accurate snapshots when per cpu drift may blur watermark comparison, succeeding on any zone watermark success and vacuously succeeding when no managed zone exists.

Reclaim under compaction continues only in compaction mode with forward progress, stopping when allocation can already succeed or compaction is already suitable, otherwise continuing while inactive file plus conditionally reclaimable anonymous pages exceed the compaction gap.

The low level suitability test adds a gap for the order and an extra low minus min margin for costly orders, then checks order zero watermarks with migration target allowance restricted by the caller zone ceiling.

A watermark suitable zone can still be rejected for costly orders when a fragmentation index is within a tunable threshold, distinguishing lack of memory from fragmentation, while cheaper orders bypass that threshold for stability.
Helpfulness of a per cgroup vector is judged from swappiness adjusted evictable size, scaled down by current priority when the cgroup is online and taken unscaled otherwise, treated as a boolean.

A memcg shrinker reporting empty clears its presence bit, issues an ordering barrier, then re-probes once; a persistent empty contributes zero while a newly non-empty result restores the presence bit to avoid losing concurrent additions.

Detachment skips already unhashed vectors, removes hashed ones with reference counted protection, decrements the owning generation count, and increments the shared sequence only when the drained generation is the current generation.

The walk chooses a random starting bin within the generation, skips entries whose generation no longer matches, and after a full cycle either returns on completed traversal or restarts when racing with rotation left a non-null terminator or a sequence mismatch.
Shrinker identity is a linear function of unit index scaled by unit width plus bit offset, and memcg bin stepping wraps modulo the bin count.

Global shrink holds read side protection only while walking the registry and acquiring a counted reference, drops it across the potentially sleeping per-shrinker work, then reacquires it before releasing the reference so neither current nor next registry element can disappear during traversal.

Memcg shrink protects registry metadata with read side sections around info lookup and identifier lookup, releases protection across sleeping shrink work, uses counted references for shrinker lifetime, and restarts metadata lookup after each shrink because expansion may have replaced the info.

Per cgroup deferred claim and return dereference per-node shrinker metadata under read side protection, then perform atomic exchange or atomic add return on the indexed per-shrinker counter selected by identifier derived index and offset.

Generation list traversal holds read side protection while fetching and reference counting each cgroup, drops it while invoking the per-vector shrink that may sleep, then reacquires it to test abort and to defer rotation until after the walk or after acquiring the next element.
Detachment serializes each node list mutation and count update with an interrupt disabling spin section, testing hashed state inside the section and releasing before moving to the next node.

Observed control block carries allocation mask, node identity and cgroup context into counting, plus scan budget and scanned accounting around each scan callback, with budget clamped to the smaller of batch size and remaining work.

Observed shrinker state includes batch and cost hints, flags for NUMA awareness memcg awareness and non-slab behavior, count and scan callbacks, deferred counters, registry linkage and numeric identity; per cgroup metadata holds per-node info with unit arrays, presence bitmaps and deferred counters indexed by identity.

Per-vector outcome first enforces cgroup protection with young signaling for below minimum and tail signaling for below low outside the tail, then after slab and pressure work returns young when rotation is requested on an online cgroup, success when no rotation is needed on a sizable vector, otherwise a single retry distinguishing tail from young by current segment.

Per-element rotation is deferred until the next element or the end of the walk, references are released before fetching the next candidate, abort breaks the walk immediately, and completion is recognized only through null list termination with matching generation value.

One configuration of the generation based node shrink entry is a compile time failure rather than an implementation, so invoking that path in that build is a build break and callers must select the alternate configuration.

Free page readings may use cached counters unless a per-zone drift mark indicates the value is close enough to blur watermark comparison, in which case an accurate snapshot is required for the balance decision.

Stale or inapplicable bitmap entries are cleared without shrink work when identifier lookup or reference acquisition fails and when kernel memory accounting is offline for slab-only shrinkers, preventing repeated useless probes.
Constants SHRINK_EMPTY, SHRINK_STOP, SHRINK_BATCH and SHRINKER_UNIT_BITS govern empty signaling, early stop, default batching and bitmap geometry for the shrinker subsystem.
Constants DEF_PRIORITY and MIN_LRU_BATCH gate initial priority estimation, with the estimate clamped between half default and default.
Constants MEMCG_LRU_YOUNG, MEMCG_LRU_TAIL and MEMCG_NR_BINS plus the segment field encode protection and rotation outcomes and generation binning for cgroup reclaim.

Constants NR_INACTIVE_FILE, NR_INACTIVE_ANON, NR_FREE_PAGES, NR_FREE_PAGES_BLOCKS, ALLOC_CMA, PAGE_ALLOC_COSTLY_ORDER and NUMA_BALANCING_MEMORY_TIERING select reclaimable accounting, free page views, migration allowance, costly threshold and tiered marking.
